name: Long Call Condor
summary: Four calls at four ascending strikes - buy the lowest, sell the two middles, buy the highest - for a net debit; a butterfly with a flat top, profiting if the underlying finishes between the middle strikes.

legs.strike_rule: strike B = A + W1, roughly 0.55 delta
strike C = B + body width (body straddles spot), roughly 0.40 delta
strike D = C + W1 (outer widths equal: D - C = B - A)

max_profit: (W1 - net debit) x 100, where W1 = B - A = D - C; realized between B and C
max_loss: net debit x 100, outside A and D
breakevens: A + net debit; D - net debit (per share)

greeks.delta: near zero when the body is centered on spot

when_to_use: Range-bound expectation with IV rank >= 30. Economically the same payoff as an iron condor at the same strikes; choose whichever is priced better (compare the call condor debit to the equivalent iron condor credit: debit + IC credit should equal W1; take the cheaper side).
entry_rules: Net debit <= 45% of W1 (outer wing width)
Body (B to C) centered within 0.25 x body width of spot; body width >= 0.75 x expected move
Outer widths equal: B - A == D - C
All four strikes with OI >= 500 and spread <= 10% of mid
Price check against the equivalent iron condor and the put condor at the same strikes; route the cheapest of the three
management_rules: Take profit at 50% of max profit ((W1 - debit) x 0.50)
Time stop at 14 DTE - condors need time to converge but gamma near expiry is dangerous with two short legs
Loss stop: close at 50% of the debit lost
If spot leaves the A-D range, close; the structure is at max loss and further waiting only adds assignment risk
exit_rules: Force-close the whole structure by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always

Close immediately if either short strike (B or C) goes ITM by more than 0.25 x W1, or a short delta >= 0.85, or short extrinsic < $0.10 - note strike B is ITM at entry by construction, so this structure requires active monitoring from day one
Ex-dividend guard: both shorts are calls; if either short call's extrinsic < projected dividend, close before the ex-date close
Never carry the ITM short call (strike B) over an ex-dividend date
assignment_risk: High relative to an iron condor: the lower short call (B) is typically ITM or near-ITM for the entire life of the trade, and short calls carry dividend-driven early assignment. This is the main practical reason to prefer the iron condor expression of the same payoff.
buying_power: Net debit x 100 per contract (all shorts covered by longs at wider strikes).
liquidity_needs: Four strikes, all penny-wide; ITM call strikes often have wider markets - check the ITM leg specifically.
common_mistakes: Ignoring that the payoff equals an iron condor and overpaying; ignoring dividend assignment on the ITM short call; body too narrow to be reachable.
zero_dte_notes: Avoid. An ITM short call on expiration day is an assignment waiting to happen, and the all-call construction has no offsetting benefit over a 0DTE iron condor.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
